items.headline: Rescued bonded labourers must get aid within a week
items.text: The Supreme Court said rescued bonded labourers should ordinarily get Rs 20,000 immediate aid within seven days of their release certificate, and that pending criminal cases are no reason to withhold it.
items.slide: Supreme Court deadline for rescued bonded labourers' aid

items.headline: Pulwama man's 15-month detention quashed
items.text: The J&K High Court quashed the Public Safety Act detention of a Pulwama man held since July 2025, saying alleged use of an encrypted app was no adequate basis for detention.
items.slide: J&K High Court quashes a Pulwama man's PSA detention

photo.alt: A narrow alley between tall brick houses with wooden windows and tangled wires overhead; a woman in a headscarf stands in the shade.
photo.caption: An alley in Srinagar's old city in 2016. The Public Safety Act is the main preventive detention law in Jammu and Kashmir.

items.headline: High Court takes up killings of lawyers
items.text: Karnataka's High Court opened a public-interest case on violence against lawyers, including two murders in October, and asked the state how it handles lawyers' complaints against police.
items.slide: Karnataka High Court opens a case on lawyers' killings

photo.alt: A large red colonnaded building with a triangular pediment behind a fence and gardens.
photo.caption: The High Court of Karnataka in Bengaluru (Attara Kacheri), in 2019.

items.figcap: to suspension and a murder case
items.headline: Officer who fired on villagers suspended, murder case filed
items.text: Bihar police suspended an officer who fired on villagers in Madhubani, killing one, and registered a murder case the same day. He has not been arrested.
items.slide: Bihar officer who fired on villagers faces a murder case

photo.alt: A railway platform whose walls are covered in colourful Mithila paintings, with red chairs and a few people.
photo.caption: Madhubani railway station, Bihar, decorated with Mithila paintings, in 2021.

items.headline: Court orders release of man held after bail
items.slide: Supreme Court orders release of a man jailed after bail
items.text: The Supreme Court ordered the immediate release of a man held weeks after it granted bail, and asked Uttar Pradesh why he should not be compensated. The state has until 3 December to reply.

photo.alt: A domed red and cream building with an Indian flag, behind trees and a black statue on a pedestal.
photo.caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi.

items.headline: Case over a misspoken slogan quashed
items.slide: Karnataka court quashes case over a 2022 rally slogan
items.text: Karnataka's High Court quashed a case over a slogan shouted at a 2022 Mandya rally, saying continuing it would abuse the legal process and no unrest was shown.

photo.alt: A large red colonnaded building with a triangular pediment behind a fence and gardens.
photo.caption: The High Court of Karnataka in Bengaluru (Attara Kacheri), in 2019.

items.headline: Detention clock starts when liberty is taken
items.slide: Supreme Court: 24-hour limit runs from detention
items.text: The Supreme Court ruled the 24-hour limit to bring a detained person before a magistrate runs from detention, not formal arrest, and freed four men in a Tripura drug case. The case against them continues.

photo.alt: A domed red and cream building with an Indian flag, behind trees and a black statue on a pedestal.
photo.caption: The Supreme Court of India in New Delhi, in 2019.

items.headline: Man freed; officer to face FIR over papers
items.place: Allahabad High Court · Farrukhabad, Uttar Pradesh
items.slide: Court finds arrest grounds were added afterwards
items.text: The Allahabad High Court freed Mohd Yaseen, finding grounds were added to his arrest papers later, and ordered an FIR against the officer. The state says the grounds were supplied; no FIR is reported yet.

photo.alt: A large cream stone court building with a pediment, red-tiled roofs and an Indian flag, behind lawns and potted plants.
photo.caption: The Allahabad High Court building in Prayagraj, in 2009.

items.headline: Worker beaten by police gets compensation
items.slide: Kerala pays ₹1 lakh to worker hit by a police officer
items.text: After a rights commission order, Kerala paid ₹1 lakh to construction worker Suresh, assaulted by a Varkala sub-inspector in 2022; the officer has repaid it. He says Suresh was arrested over illegal soil digging.

items.headline: Court quashes NSA detention of Kaziranga activist
items.place: Gauhati High Court · Kaziranga, Golaghat, Assam
items.slide: Court: Doley was held on "stale" cases
items.text: The Gauhati High Court quashed Pranab Doley's NSA detention after 115+ days, finding it rested on "stale" cases; he was set to be released. Assam had cited foreign visits and funds; three cases remain live.

photo.alt: Tall grass in the foreground and a lone tree on flat grassland under a blue sky.
photo.caption: Grassland in Kaziranga National Park, Assam, near the hotel site Doley protested against, in 2023.

items.headline: Four Siang dam protesters freed
items.place: Jully Central Jail, Itanagar · Geku, Upper Siang, Arunachal Pradesh
items.slide: Four Siang villagers freed; six others still held
items.text: Four Geku villagers held since 9 October under Arunachal's anti-terror law were freed as a state "goodwill gesture" before talks. Six others remain detained, and their cases have not been withdrawn.

photo.alt: A wide river with sandbanks and a long bridge, seen between forested hills, under a cloudy sky.
photo.caption: The Siang river near Pasighat, downstream of Upper Siang where the four villagers live, in 2023.

items.headline: Pranab Doley walks out of jail
items.slide: Kaziranga activist freed after 118 days in custody
items.text: Land-rights activist Pranab Doley left Golaghat jail on 6 November after the High Court quashed his NSA detention. Three cases against him remain live; no Assam government response was reported.

photo.alt: Tall grass in the foreground and a lone tree on flat grassland under a blue sky.
photo.caption: Grassland in Kaziranga National Park, Assam, near the hotel site Doley protested against, in 2023.

items.headline: Journalist freed after five days without charge
items.text: Israel released Palestinian journalist Abed Abou Shhadeh after five days' detention without charge. His lawyers say the suspicion rested on a public podcast conversation; no official comment was reported.
items.slide: Abed Abou Shhadeh released after 5 days, no charge filed

photo.alt: A tall sandstone clock tower with a green spire beside a cream building with balconies, under a blue sky.
photo.caption: The clock tower in Jaffa, where Abou Shhadeh lives, in 2015.

items.headline: Law students run legal aid camps in Bengaluru slums
items.text: Alliance School of Law and the NGO MAARGA held five legal aid camps near Jayanagar and published residents' problems with pensions, ration cards and certificates. Whether officials will act is not yet reported.
items.slide: 5 camps help Bengaluru slum residents claim entitlements

items.headline: Two men acquitted after six years under UAPA
items.text: A special court acquitted two Baramulla men jailed since 2020, finding police evidence of an arms recovery inconsistent. The six years cannot be returned; any appeal is not yet reported.
items.slide: Court finds police evidence unreliable in Baramulla

photo.alt: A long suspension footbridge with metal railings stretching into thick fog.
photo.caption: A suspension footbridge in Baramulla on a foggy morning, in 2023.

items.headline: Court presses UP to free prisoners already granted bail
items.text: The Supreme Court ordered UP to identify undertrials granted bail but jailed over surety conditions, saying release is the state's duty. 106 such prisoners were found in 20 districts; 55 remain unchecked.
items.slide: SC orders UP to trace 'bailed but jailed' prisoners

items.headline: Court strikes down Trinidad's same-sex conduct laws
items.text: The Privy Council unanimously held two sections criminalising consensual same-sex conduct unconstitutional, in a case brought by Jason Jones. A final order on the law's wording is still to come.
items.slide: Privy Council strikes down Trinidad same-sex conduct laws

items.headline: Court: inviting public debate is not enmity
items.text: The Sikkim High Court quashed an FIR and chargesheet over an invitation to a public consultation on Darjeeling-Sikkim unification, holding it did not promote enmity. The state may still appeal.
items.slide: Sikkim HC quashes FIR over a public consultation invite

items.headline: Prosecution of two IAS officers sanctioned
items.text: The Centre sanctioned prosecuting two IAS officers in a road-tender corruption case after Madras High Court pressure. The court will monitor the probe; no charges have been framed yet and the accused can contest them.
items.slide: Centre sanctions case against two IAS officers in Chennai

items.headline: Court upholds payout over inmate's suicide
items.text: Tripura High Court ruled the rights commission's order binding: ₹4 lakh compensation and action against officials over a 2024 inmate suicide. The state, citing an inquiry clearing staff, has a month to comply.
items.slide: Tripura court orders payout over inmate's death in jail

items.headline: Two riot police jailed for assaulting protester
items.text: A Tbilisi court jailed two riot police officers for five years each for assaulting protester Zviad Maisashvili at 2024 pro-EU rallies, and barred them from posts for three years. No ministry comment was reported.
items.slide: Georgian court jails two riot officers for beating protester
